(a) 
Report on Part-Time Employment.—
        (1) 
Section 3407 of title 5, United States Code, is repealed.
 
        (2) 
The table of sections for chapter 34 of title 5, United States Code, is amended by striking out the item relating to section 3407.
  
    (b) 
Semiannual Report on Lobbying.—Section 1352 of title 31, United States Code, is amended by—

        (1) 
striking out subsection (d); and
 
        (2) 
redesignating subsections (e), (f), (g), and (h) as subsections (d), (e), (f), and (g), respectively.
  
    (c) 
Reports on Program Fraud and Civil Remedies.—
        (1) 
Section 3810 of title 31, United States Code, is repealed.
 
        (2) 
The table of sections for chapter 38 of title 31, United States Code, is amended by striking out the item relating to section 3810.
  
    (d) 
Report on Right to Financial Privacy Act.—Section 1121 of the Right to Financial Privacy Act of 1978 (12 U.S.C. 3421) is repealed.
 
    (e) 
Report on Plans to Convert to the Metric System.—Section 12 of the Metric Conversion Act of 1975 (15 U.S.C. 205j–1) is repealed.
 
    (f) 
Report on Technology Utilization and Intellectual Property Rights.—Section 11(f) of the Stevenson-Wydler Technology Innovation Act of 1980 (15 U.S.C. 3710(f)) is repealed.
 
    (g) 
Report on Extraordinary Contractual Actions To Facilitate the National Defense.—Section 4(a) of the Act entitled “An Act to authorize the making, amendment, and modification of contracts to facilitate the national defense”, approved August 28, 1958 (50 U.S.C. 1434(a)), is amended by striking out “all such actions taken” and inserting in lieu thereof “if any such action has been taken”.
 
    (h) 
Reports on Detailing Employees.—Section 619 of the Treasury, Postal Service, and General Government Appropriations  Act, 1993 (Public Law 102–393; 106 Stat. 1769), is repealed.

fable.w: The section only repeals or amends various statutory reporting requirements, such as reports on part-time employment, lobbying, program fraud and metric conversion. The tempting reading is that words like "Lobbying" or "Reports" signal outside involvement, but these are housekeeping repeals of reports that stay inside the federal government. Nothing here creates a comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or a right to sue.
fable.s: Section 3810 of title 31, United States Code, is repealed.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of repeals and amendments to existing statutory provisions regarding reports. It does not establish any new requirement for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The repealed sections generally involved reports to Congress or internal agency reporting, which are not considered participation under the definition. Therefore, there is no participation involved.
qwen_block.s: (a) Report on Part-Time Employment.— (1) Section 3407 of title 5, United States Code, is repealed.
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that repealing sections that required reports implies removing a form of participation or oversight. However, the definition of participation requires active consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties *before* a decision is made. This section merely lists the repeal or amendment of existing statutory provisions regarding reports. It does not establish any new process for outside parties to participate in federal decision-making. Furthermore, reports to Congress (which are inside the government) are explicitly excluded from the definition of participation. Since this section only removes old reporting requirements and does not create new mechanisms for outside involvement, it is not participation.

opus.w: This section only repeals or changes reporting requirements, such as reports on part-time employment, lobbying, program fraud and metric conversion. Those reports are internal to the government or go to Congress, which counts as inside the federal government. Words like "Lobbying" or "Contractual Actions" appear only as report titles. The section creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside groups, or right to sue.
opus.s:
Semiannual Report on Lobbying.—Section 1352 of title 31, United States Code, is amended by—

striking out subsection (d)
opus.b: The tempting reading is to see "Lobbying," "Right to Financial Privacy," or "Contractual Actions" and assume outside parties are involved. That doesn't hold up. Each subsection only repeals or narrows a reporting requirement, and those reports go to Congress or stay inside the government. No one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of repeals and amendments to reporting requirements for federal agencies. It does not establish any process for consultation, comment, or participation by non-federal entities. The reports mentioned are internal government communications or reports to Congress, which are inside the federal government boundary.
qwen_chat.s: (a) Report on Part-Time Employment.— (1) Section 3407 of title 5, United States Code, is repealed.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it involves reports, which might imply public input.
Resolution: The section only repeals or amends requirements for federal agencies to submit reports to Congress or other federal entities. It does not create any mechanism for outside parties to participate in decision-making.
